record.experiment_description:
Objectives:

NIH.R3 was a proof-of-concept experiment, designed to test the capability of the Animal Enclosure Module Nursing Facility (AEM-NF) in preparation for the upcoming Neurolab (STS-90) mission. The goals of the hardware verification test were to verify the survival of rat dams and neonates in an AEM with a Nursing Facility (NF) insert for the duration of the flight, to verify that clinically healthy animals are retrieved post flight, and to evaluate the maternal behaviors of the rat dams in the AEM NF cages throughout the shuttle mission.

Approach:

Six litters of Sprague-Dawley rats were used in the experiment. Each litter consisted of one nursing dam and 10 neonates, with two identically-aged litters per AEM-NF. Two litters (in one AEM-NF) each were launched with neonate ages at Post Natal day 5 (PN%), Post Natal day 8 (PN8), and Post Natal day 15 (PN15). PN5 was the first choice for launch age for Neurolab. PN8 was second choice, and PN15 was last choice. In-flight activities consisted of daily health checks, water refill, and videotaping of the animals. Post-flight, animals were removed from the AEM-NF and assessed for survival rate and health.

Results:

Only 6 out of the 20 PN5 neonates survived the flight. Of the PN8 neonates, 19 out of 20 survived and all of the PN15 neonates survived. All flight groups weighed less than the corresponding ground controls, although there may have been a significant cage effect independent of gravity or microgravity. All surviving flight animals were in good or very good condition as described by the inspecting veterinarian. The AEM-NF proved to be suitable for the support of rat neonates aged PN8 or older at launch, but unsuitable for the support of those PN5 or younger at launch. However, because of the sample size of only 2 dams, it is inconclusive whether the poor survival in the PN5 group could have been due to poor dam behavior.
